# lib/application.js:194  (lib.application.use)
```typescript
(local function) use(fn: any, ...args: any[]): typeof module.exports
```
Proxy `Router#use()` to add middleware to the app router.
See Router#use() documentation for details.

If the _fn_ parameter is an express app, then it will be
mounted at the _route_ specified.

# lib/application.js:144  (lib.application.lazyrouter)
```typescript
(local function) lazyrouter(): void
```
lazily adds the base router if it has not yet been added.

We cannot add the base router in the defaultConfiguration because
it reads app settings which might be set after that has run.

*@private*

## Task

You are investigating how Express mounts middleware in lib/application.js. Starting from `use`, trace the exact causal pipeline that runs when middleware is mounted on an application for the first time: what triggers the application's internal router to be lazily constructed, and what real configuration lookups happen along the way.

First give a short (2-4 sentence) explanation of the pipeline.

Then, on its own line, emit a fenced JSON code block containing an ordered array of the fully-qualified symbol names in that causal order - only symbols actually present in the provided context package may appear, e.g.:

```json
["lib.application.use", "lib.application.lazyrouter"]
```


## Response format

Respond with a single fenced JSON object and nothing else:
```json
{"reasoning": "<short explanation>", "symbols": ["<fully.qualified.name>", "..."]}
```
`symbols` lists every code symbol that is part of your answer, in order, by exact fully-qualified name.
